title.narrative: Guinea-Bissau Reform Advancement Development Policy Financing

description.narrative: The development objective is to: (i) strengthen public financial management and domestic resource mobilization; (ii) enhance energy and water utility viability and digital growth.

The development objective of the Reform Advancement Development Policy Financing for Guinea-Bissau is to: (i) strengthen public financial management and domestic resource mobilization; and (ii) enhance energy and water utility viability and digital growth. The prior action (PAs) and result indicators of the operation are directly linked to the New World Bank Group (WBG) Scorecard Indicators. These indicators are: (i) a target of tax revenue equal to or higher than 15 percent of gross domestic product (GDP); (ii) GW of renewable energy capacity enabled; (iii) the percentage of the population with access to electricity; (iv) percentage of the population using the internet; and (v) state of online e-government service provision.

title.narrative: Tax revenue as a percentage of GDP

comment.narrative: In 2025, tax revenue increased to 8.5 percent of GDP, up from 8.1 percent in 2024, driven primarily by stronger VAT collections (+0.2 percentage points of GDP) and higher export taxes (+0.2 percentage points of GDP). Revised data for 2023 indicate a lower baseline, with tax revenue now estimated at 8.5 percent of GDP in 2023. In nominal terms, tax revenue rose by 15 percent in 2025, reflecting in part a 29 percent increase in VAT receipts following the replacement of the previous consumption tax.

title.narrative: Share of public expenditures executed through the TSA, including wage bill payments

comment.narrative: The TSA is not yet fully operational. As an interim measure, all transactions executed directly by the Treasury through its Central Bank of West African States (Banque Centrale des Etats de l’Afrique de l’Ouest , BCEAO) account are treated as TSA transactions. On this basis, public expenditures processed via the Treasury's BCEAO account currently for 27.5 percent.

title.narrative: Operating deficit of the national utility company Electricity and Water of Guinea-Bissau (EAGB) as a percentage of revenue.

comment.narrative: The target has been exceeded. Through the SESAP project, international experts were hired to manage the utility. The SESAP project team reported that effective management performance and initiatives, including successful client debt recovery and the implementation of pre-paid meters have led to increased revenue and reduced commercial losses. Combined with a reduction in generation costs, the utility shifted from a deficit of approximately 50% to achieving a positive monthly balance (starting June 2025).

title.narrative: Price of a data-only 2GB mobile-broadband basket (% of monthly GNI per capita)

comment.narrative: The latest data available (November 2025) indicates that the target has been exceeded. The publication of Decree No. 06/2025 on March 12, 2025, signaled the Government's commitment to a competitive and efficiently managed wholesale market, leading to a decrease of the price. In 2025, the ITU revised the definition of the indicator to “price of a data only 5GB mobile broadband basket,” making the original results indicator no longer directly comparable over time. Based on the new definition, performance has improved markedly, with the price of a data only 5GB mobile broadband basket (as a percentage of monthly GNI per capita) declining from 17.1 percent in 2024 to 10.2 percent in 2025. Data source: https://www.itu.int/en/ITU-D/Statistics/Pages/ICTprices/default.aspx.

title.narrative: The frequency the of online publication of consolidated and audited fiscal reports

comment.narrative: The government published semiannual reports on budget execution, consolidated fiscal/non-fiscal revenues, and cashflow forecasts validated by the Treasury Committee covering the first and second semester of 2025 on the website of the Ministry of Finance. The website architecture of the MoF has been adapted to facilitate future publications, in line with Ministerial Orders 147/GMF/2024 of December 18, 2024, and 05/GMF/2025 of February 7, 2025. No annual financial audits of these reports have been conducted by the Court of Accounts.
